# XxHash64

xxHash64 over a stream of bytes, in as many writes as the caller has.

```rux
pub struct XxHash64 {
    // private fields
}
```

Copy, but large: thirty-two bytes of pending input plus its accumulators. Borrow one by reference unless a
snapshot of the hash so far is what is wanted.

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>XxHash64</code></h3>

```rux
pub func XxHash64() -> XxHash64
```

Constructs an unseeded hasher with nothing written into it yet.

**Returns**: a hasher with a seed of zero

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L148)

## Associated functions

<h3 id="with-seed"><code>WithSeed</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WithSeed(seed: uint64) -> XxHash64
```

A hasher with nothing written into it yet, using `seed`.
`seed` is read by value. Two hashers with different seeds give unrelated answers for the same input, which is
enough to keep accidental collisions from following data from one table to another. It is not enough to stop
a deliberate collision: an adversary who knows the seed is no worse off than one hashing without it.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

| Name   | Type     | Description            |
| ------ | -------- | ---------------------- |
| `seed` | `uint64` | the seed to start from |

**Returns**: a hasher seeded with it

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L160)

## Methods

<h3 id="reset"><code>Reset</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Reset(self: &var XxHash64)
```

Puts the hasher back to where it started, keeping its seed.
`self` is borrowed mutably. Everything written so far is forgotten; the seed is not.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L177)

## Implements Hasher

`XxHash64` conforms to [`Hasher`](/docs/api/hash/hasher).

<h3 id="write"><code>Write</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Write(self: &var XxHash64, bytes: *byte, length: uint)
```

Adds `length` bytes at `bytes` to the hash.
`bytes` is borrowed and read; `length` is read by value. A zero length changes nothing and is the one case in
which `bytes` may be null. Input that does not fill a block is held until the rest of it arrives, so any
division of the same byte stream into writes gives the same answer.
Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`bytes` must be readable for `length` bytes.

| Name     | Type    | Description                          |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `bytes`  | `*byte` | the bytes to absorb                  |
| `length` | `uint`  | how many bytes; zero absorbs nothing |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L206)

<h3 id="finish"><code>Finish</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Finish(self: &var XxHash64) -> uint64
```

The hash of everything written so far.
`self` is borrowed. Nothing is consumed: asking twice gives the same answer, and writing more continues from
where the writes left off rather than starting over.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to what is held pending, which is under one block. Allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the hash of everything written since the last reset

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L255)

<h3 id="xx-block-size"><code>XxBlockSize</code></h3>

```rux
pub const XxBlockSize: uint = 32;
```

How many bytes one xxHash64 round consumes: four lanes of eight.
An input shorter than this never touches the accumulators at all, which is why the short and long paths give
different-looking code for the same algorithm.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L44)

<h3 id="read-little-endian64"><code>ReadLittleEndian64</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ReadLittleEndian64(bytes: *byte) -> uint64
```

The eight bytes at `bytes` as a 64-bit value, least significant byte first.
`bytes` is borrowed and read. Assembled a byte at a time rather than read as a word, so the answer is the same at
any address on any machine — xxHash is defined on a little-endian byte stream, not on whatever the machine
happens to hold.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.
`bytes` must be readable for eight bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L55)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description         |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `*byte` | eight bytes to read |

**Returns**: them as a little-endian word

<h3 id="read-little-endian32"><code>ReadLittleEndian32</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ReadLittleEndian32(bytes: *byte) -> uint32
```

The four bytes at `bytes` as a 32-bit value, least significant byte first.
`bytes` is borrowed and read. Assembled a byte at a time, for the same reason as [`ReadLittleEndian64`](/docs/api/hash/xx-hash64#read-little-endian64).
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.
`bytes` must be readable for four bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L72)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description        |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------ |
| `bytes` | `*byte` | four bytes to read |

**Returns**: them as a little-endian half word

<h3 id="xx-round"><code>XxRound</code></h3>

```rux
pub func XxRound(accumulator: uint64, lane: uint64) -> uint64
```

One accumulator round: mix `lane` into `accumulator`.
Both are read by value and the new accumulator is returned. This is the whole of xxHash64's inner loop — scale
the input, add, rotate, scale again — and it is what the four lanes each run independently.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L90)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type     | Description                    |
| ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| `accumulator` | `uint64` | the lane's running value       |
| `lane`        | `uint64` | the input word to fold into it |

**Returns**: the lane's new value

<h3 id="xx-merge"><code>XxMerge</code></h3>

```rux
pub func XxMerge(hash: uint64, accumulator: uint64) -> uint64
```

Folds one finished accumulator into the running hash.
Both are read by value and the new hash is returned. The accumulator is passed through a round from zero first,
so a lane that happened to end at a convenient value does not stay convenient.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L102)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type     | Description               |
| ------------- | -------- | ------------------------- |
| `hash`        | `uint64` | the running hash          |
| `accumulator` | `uint64` | the lane to merge into it |

**Returns**: the merged hash

<h3 id="xx-avalanche"><code>XxAvalanche</code></h3>

```rux
pub func XxAvalanche(hash: uint64) -> uint64
```

The final mixing step, which spreads every input bit across the whole result.
`hash` is read by value and the finished hash is returned. Without this a one-bit change in the input moves only
the bits the round function reached; with it, about half of them move.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L114)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type     | Description      |
| ------ | -------- | ---------------- |
| `hash` | `uint64` | the value to mix |

**Returns**: it with every input bit spread across the output

<h3 id="xx-hash64-seeded-of"><code>XxHash64SeededOf</code></h3>

```rux
pub func XxHash64SeededOf(bytes: *byte, length: uint, seed: uint64) -> uint64
```

The xxHash64 of `length` bytes at `bytes`, using `seed`.
`bytes` is borrowed and read; `length` and `seed` are read by value. A zero length gives the hash of the empty
input for that seed, and is the one case in which `bytes` may be null.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`bytes` must be readable for `length` bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/XxHash.rux#L304)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type     | Description            |
| -------- | -------- | ---------------------- |
| `bytes`  | `*byte`  | the bytes to hash      |
| `length` | `uint`   | how many bytes         |
| `seed`   | `uint64` | the seed to start from |

**Returns**: their seeded hash

pub func XxHash64Of(bytes: *byte, length: uint) -> uint64

The xxHash64 of `length` bytes at `bytes`, seeded with zero.

Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
